carousels.name: 5 bedtime rules if p*rn keeps you up at night (59% insomnia odds)

slides.title: 5 bedtime rules if p*rn keeps you [[up at night.]]
slides.sub: Every extra hour on a screen in bed: 59% higher odds of insomnia.

slides.title: Higher [[insomnia]] odds
slides.body: In a study of ~40,000 Norwegian students (Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2025), each extra hour of screen time after going to bed was tied to 59% higher odds of insomnia symptoms. That's screens in general — p*rn in bed adds a second problem.

slides.title: Rules [[1–2]]
items: Screens off 30 minutes before bed.
Your phone charges across the room, not on the pillow.

slides.title: Rules [[3–5]]
items: Same bedtime, even on weekends.
Bed is for sleep — no scrolling, no p*rn, no "just checking."
Can't sleep in 20 minutes? Get up and read until you're drowsy.

slides.title: Start [[tonight]]
items: Set a bedtime alarm, not just a wake-up alarm.
Get a cheap alarm clock so the phone can leave.
Keep a paper book on the nightstand.
Note how you sleep for a week.
slides.note: Save this and try it tonight 🔖

Sleep better.

slides.lead: Guided sleep audio, a p*rn blocker for late nights and streaks for every night you stay off it.

carousels.name: 5 stages of quitting p*rn and where many people give up

slides.title: 5 stages of quitting p*rn [[— and where many people give up.]]
slides.sub: Find your stage. Then push through it.

slides.title: The [[decision]]
slides.body: You're sick of p*rn. You promise yourself this is the last time. Easy to start. Easy to restart.

slides.title: Stages [[2–3]]
items: The honeymoon: a few good days. You feel unstoppable.
The wall: boredom, urges, bargaining. Many people go back to p*rn here.

slides.title: Stages [[4–5]]
items: The rebuild: new routines start to feel normal.
The new normal: p*rn stops being the first thing you reach for.

slides.title: Get past [[the wall]]
items: Expect it — it's a stage, not proof you've failed.
Lean on people hardest at this point.
Change your evenings, not just your rules.
Count weeks, not days.
slides.note: Which stage are you in? Comment 1–5 👇

Get past the wall.

slides.lead: A step-by-step p*rn recovery program, accountability with real people and a panic button for the hard stage.

carousels.name: 4 reasons 'I'll restart in December' keeps you stuck (NNN, harsh)

slides.title: 4 reasons "I'll restart in December" [[keeps you stuck in p*rn.]]
slides.sub: Slipped this week? Don't write off the last 8 days.

slides.title: It's a [[free pass]]
slides.body: "I'll restart Dec 1" really means 8 more days of p*rn with no rules. That's not a reset. That's a binge with a plan.

slides.title: Binges [[cost]] more
slides.body: A slip is one night. Eight days of "who cares" p*rn digs the habit deeper. Stopping now is easier than stopping later.

slides.title: Reasons [[3–4]]
items: December won't be easier — holidays, time off, late nights.
You've done this before. How many "fresh starts" have you had?
